text: Ooh, look how brown that got. So why doesn't boiled meat ever look like this?
That browning? It's not actually from oxygen.

It's heat that makes the protein and sugar in meat fuse together into brand-new compounds - the ones that give it that color and smell. That reaction is named after the chemist who first figured it out - it's called the Maillard reaction.
But this reaction needs serious heat to kick in, and boiling water simply can't get that hot.
That's why patting meat dry before you cook it helps it brown better. If the surface is still wet, the temperature can't climb past 100°C until that water's gone.
The same thing browns your toast, and it's what darkens coffee beans when they're roasted.
That's why grilled meat turns brown, and boiled meat never does.
